o1.biggest_strength: It correctly builds the flow around the main signals: dark spots lead, beginners need a slow-start plan, and sunscreen needs white-cast and stickiness objections answered.
o1.biggest_mistake: It uses the banned word “brightening” even as a contrast, and Email 5 pushes the same salicylic-acid-led 3-step routine to everyone instead of keeping the routine matched to the quiz concern.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep every product recommendation segmented through the last email, remove banned language, and tighten the final routine so dark spots get niacinamide plus SPF while oily skin gets salicylic plus SPF.

o2.biggest_strength: It is sharply built from the data, especially the niacinamide/dark-spots opportunity, the sunscreen conversion leak, and the beginner fear of actives.
o2.biggest_mistake: The WhatsApp template says to use the matched product every other night, which is wrong for the sunscreen segment and needs conditional copy.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add conditional WhatsApp wording for sunscreen users and make the final reminder link directly to the matched routine rather than a broad best-sellers page.

reason: Both are usable, but Output 2 is the one I would rather run because it is more tightly segmented, has better Klaviyo flow logic, and adds useful measurement thinking without losing the brand voice. Output 1 is strong, but the banned word and the generic final 3-step routine make it need more cleanup.
